title: The Night Watch
source: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam (public domain: Rembrandt died in 1669). Wikimedia Commons: The Night Watch - cropped.jpg, 28302x23662, saved at 8000 px.
caption: Everyone calls it The Night Watch. It isn't night, and someone is hiding in it. #art #arthistory #painting #rembrandt #museum
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-11 (Wikipedia; Rijksmuseum '10 things about Rembrandt's Night Watch'): official title 'Militia Company of District II under the Command of Captain Frans Banninck Cocq', 1642, Rijksmuseum; name 'Night Watch' only from 1797, due to dark varnish (removed in the 1940s); 1715 moved to the Town Hall on the Dam and cut on all four sides to fit between two doors, largest piece from the left, two figures lost, never recovered; girl with dead chicken on her belt, claws refer to the kloveniers/clauweniers; captain's hand shadow falls on lieutenant Willem van Ruytenburch's coat with Amsterdam's coat of arms; three musketeers show loading, firing, cleaning; attacked 1911, 1975 (12 cuts, bread knife), 1990 (acid).

Hidden face with beret and one eye: popularly said to be Rembrandt, but most modern scholarship disagrees (Bas Dudok van Heel: probably drummer Jacob Jorisz). The slide presents it as a debate, not a fact.
Payment: Wikipedia says 1,600 guilders, 100 per person, but 18 names are on the shield; numbers not used on slides.
All focus boxes: check with inspect_focus and --debug.

slides.headline: Everyone calls this The Night Watch. It isn't night.
Amsterdam, 1642
slides.text: A militia company paid Rembrandt for a group portrait. They expected neat rows. He painted them marching out.

slides.headline: The captain gives the order
slides.text: In black, Captain Frans Banninck Cocq. Beside him in gold, his lieutenant, listening.

slides.headline: Now look at his hand
slides.text: Its shadow falls on the lieutenant's coat, right around the coat of arms of Amsterdam.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, on the left
slides.text: A man in red loads his musket. Elsewhere in the crowd, others fire and clean theirs: a gun drill in three steps.

slides.headline: But who is she?
slides.text: A girl glowing in gold walks among the soldiers. And on her belt hangs a dead chicken.

slides.headline: The chicken is a clue
slides.text: Its claws stand for the company's name: the Kloveniers. She is their emblem, walking.

slides.headline: And who is hiding here?
slides.text: Behind the soldiers, a beret and one eye peek out. Many say it's Rembrandt himself. Some historians say: the drummer.

slides.headline: And the night?
slides.text: Just old, dark varnish. In 1715 the canvas was cut on all four sides to fit a wall. The pieces were never found.
